utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence had four preliminary matters to raise, the Prosecution would have two, but we'll start with one the Chamber would like to address. Next week Tuesday, that is, the 29th of September, we'll start half an hour later and continue half an hour longer; therefore, we'll sit from 10.00 to a quarter to 3.00. Mr. Ivetic, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I guess I'll go first. On this past Monday, at transcript page 39122 onwards, Your Honour asked us to provide in court today a detailed chronology as to the appointment of experts as to Tomasica and their receipt of materials and work. I provide the same as follows. On 14 July 2015, I personally forwarded lead counsel's request for appointment, authorisation to work, and funding for the Tomasica part of the case for Professor Radovanovic to act as a Defence expert, sending the same to the relevant officers within OLAD via e-mail. The request also sought approval and authorisation and funding for a trip to the OTP demographic unit by Professor Radovanovic and two assistants in order to be able to review the archives of the OTP demographic unit. Here I quote verbatim from that request. "Ms. Radovanovic is expected to analyse the foregoing evidence to identify flaws and criticisms which could be used to challenge or rebut that evidence as part of the Defence case in chief. Further, insofar as the evidence of Ms. Tabeau featured heavily on the integrated database and records that are within the Office of the Prosecution, Ms. Radovanovic's work will include the need to visit the Office of the Prosecution to work for several days with her assistants to work with this database in relation to Tabeau's reports. For this purpose, we will send you shortly the CVs of her assistants, Mr. Bozo Grbic and Ms. Slavica Pavkov. Both of them have decades of experience in the official statistical organs of the RS government. It is anticipated that they would need to travel to The Hague and work four to five days with the OTP demographers unit, and also since Ms.Tabeau's work did not take into account certain data or factors in doing her review, Ms. Radovanovic may have to seek some outside sources of information to test Dr. Tabeau's theories to see if they are sound when taking into account that missing information. This additional research includes," and then we identified a list of items. And now I quote a later part of the same Defence request. "It is thus critical to permit the Defence to have a fair opportunity to have a counter-expert review this report in evidence so as to rebut the evidence." On 16 July 2015, OLAD wrote personally to me asking for clarification if Professor Radovanovic would necessarily be preparing a report since if not, she could be named as a member of the Defence team to informally assist us with no additional funding but not to write an expert report. On 17 July 2015, I personally wrote back to OLAD advising that since Professor Radovanovic was foreseen to be preparing not only an expert report but testifying as an expert witness as to Tomasica, the option of naming her to the Defence team, rather than authorising her as an expert, was not feasible and that thus additional funding under the directive for experts was essential and required. On 21 July 2015, I received personally the preliminary decision of OLAD that the assistants of Professor Radovanovic could not be appointed nor considered for funding and were being denied funding. It was suggested that the assistants could be appointed to the Defence team and paid under the already expended Defence budget or work pro bono, with the Defence team paying out of pocket for their travel and lodging to permit such a trip. As to our pending request for appointment and funding for Professor Radovanovic, OLAD promised to let us know "as soon as practicable." It is important to note the Defence team budget is maxed out and OLAD did not increase the same for the inclusion of any experts. On 5 August 2015, after no word from OLAD, the Defence team followed up with a request for status and decision as to the outstanding requests for Professor Radovanovic and Professor Stankovic to be authorised and funded as to Tomasica, stressing the rapid movement of the case and the need to resolve the matter quickly. We again asked for funding for the assistants of Professor Radovanovic to permit them to review material at the OTP demographic unit's archives as had been permitted in other previous cases for these same assistants, providing details of those engagements and work in prior cases. On 12 August 2015, I personally forwarded lead counsel's request for appointment of Dr. Stankovic to OLAD, for purposes of Tomasica, as OLAD were unaware of the request. On 17 August 2015, the Defence team received a letter from OLAD approving the appointment as to both Professor Radovanovic and Dr. Stankovic as experts for purposes of the Tomasica evidence and granting an allocation of hours to fund the same. However, as to Professor Radovanovic's request to visit the OTP demographic unit with her assistants to perform a review of the same, again the assistants of Professor Radovanovic were denied funding with the implication that they could be assigned to the Defence team with no additional funding to work pro bono. Also, the letter made no reference whatsoever to request for Professor Radovanovic to be authorised and funded for a visit to the OTP demographic unit. Rather, the letter denied travel expenses for Professor Radovanovic to travel unless strictly necessary and cited travel to testify as being something that would be covered. The letter thus did not grant funding nor approval for Professor Radovanovic or her assistants to visit the OTP demographic unit. That issue still has not been resolved favourably. And I know quote from that OLAD letter verbatim as to travel: "Please note that the Registry does not reimburse travel expenses of experts unless strictly necessary to fulfil the scope of the assignment. Please be informed, however, that should this assigned expert be called to testify as an expert witness in court, the Tribunal's Victims and Witnesses Section will deal with the matters resulting thereof." Thus, the Registrar's assertion in their 3 September 2015 filing that they are a waiting a travel request for Professor Radovanovic is not accurate. Our original request outlined the proposed plan of travel on 14 July 2015, which the Registry has not approved in its 17 August letter, and rather we have heard the wording that I have just read above. At the very best, we are awaiting Registry approval of our request. At the very worst interpretation, it has been denied. I personally travelled to Belgrade on 19 August 2015 and met with Professor Radovanovic and with Dr. Stankovic on 20 August 2015, with my legal assistant, for purposes of conveying to them the OLAD decision and discussing the Tomasica appointment and outlining the time-frame and work required due to the dynamics of the case. I stressed to them the short time-frame and outlined the schedule for the remainder of the Defence case. Both gave their assent to accept the appointment and do their best to work under the difficult conditions and time pressure. I outlined to them the type of material that we had received from the OTP and advised them to liaise with the legal assistant to complete the signed undertaking required by OLAD and to take over the custody of the files to begin work and for any remaining questions or issues. On 21 August 2015, I was engaged in travel the better part of the day to return to The Hague, but my legal assistant met with and handed over, in electronic format, all of the disclosed demographic evidence as to Tomasica to Professor Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Already on 22 August 2015, Professor Radovanovic was required to travel to The Hague for her testimony in these proceedings as to the remainder of the Prosecution evidence. On 22 August 2015, my legal assistant met with Professor Dr. Stankovic and handed over to him, in electronic format, all of the disclosed forensic court medicine material as to Tomasica. From 22 August to 28 August 2015, Professor Radovanovic was in The Hague for purposes of testifying before Your Honours for her initial expertise as to the remainder of the Prosecution case minus Tomasica as a retained Defence expert. On 29 August 2015, I personally communicated with Professor Radovanovic who confirmed her arrival back in Belgrade from the Hague and said that she would commence her review of the Tomasica evidence in a few days after catching up with obligations that arose while in The Hague and recovering from exertions related to her travel and to her testimony. On 11 September 2015, I personally received Professor Radovanovic's signed undertaking from the assistant in the field and immediately forwarded the same to OLAD as per OLAD's request. The undertaking had been signed already on 19 August 2015. I was also advised that Professor Radovanovic needed to speak with me as to additional matters and materials she felt were needed. On 11 September 2015, I personally, with co-counsel, contacted Professor Radovanovic as to the request for additional materials that had not been disclosed by the OTP and talked about her progress and specific requests for official documentation to relevant state authorities. An official request was drafted that same day and sent out to the relevant authorities by co-counsel. To date, we have not gotten a response to the request of the relevant authorities for the required documents. Until said documents are received, it would be premature and impossible to predict accurately the amount of time that would be required for Professor Radovanovic to complete her review of the same and draft the necessary report and analysis, since we don't know the number or volume of the same. Professor Stankovic's schedule and availability have been limited of late due to his official governmental duties in relation to his governmental appointment such that I have not as of yet received his signed undertaking. However, he has confirmed that he has started to review the voluminous forensic material of the Prosecution disclosure as to Tomasica. We anticipate and have asked that he attempt to complete his review and provide a drafted report within 45 days of today, if possible. My legal assistant is trying to reach him today to try and get feedback on that proposed possibility. And that completes the detailed chronology that I have prepared. And I apologise to the translators for speaking quickly at certain points while reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have a few questions. First, of course, we'll ask the Registry to make any submissions, if they wish to do so. You said on the 14th of July you announced the CVs of the assistants of Professor Radovanovic to be provided. When did you send them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe the CVs were sent, I think, either the next day or the day after, since we already received on the 21st, which would be seven days later, the initial denial after they had reviewed the CVs. So it's sometime within that same week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Within days. Then I have -- you referred to the 21st, you said the assistants were denied. Was that also the day when the appointment of Professor Radovanovic, apart from travelling and coming to The Hague, was approved, or is that misunderstood?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, it was not. As a matter of fact, as I stated as to our request for Professor Radovanovic, OLAD in that e-mail said they would promise to let us know "as soon as practicable."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that decision arrived on the 17th of August, 2015.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do I understand that in fact until early September, Professor Radovanovic was unable to start working on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I wasn't sure if you had something to add. It sounded like you were still in the midst of a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And my last question would be, when Professor Radovanovic was in The Hague here for testimony, was it considered or has she tried to do in The Hague -- that is, to consult the underlying materials she said she would need and therefore even need to travel to The Hague to look at them when she was here, which would have resulted in one-time travel expenses serving two purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: She has. That was originally what we had proposed, that when she would come to testify she could go to the Prosecution and do the review. She has advised, of course, that she needs her assistants to perform that review, that she is not able to perform a review of the databases by herself without the assistance of statistical assistants and the type of assistants that the Prosecution experts also employed and also identified in their reports and in their testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those informations. I think the Prosecution, apart from now a reference on how the Prosecution works, is hardly involved or not involved, apart from this scheduling aspects, of course. Is there any wish to make any further submissions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I have a couple of quick comments. Number one: No, the Prosecution was, in the sense the Court means, not involved. Particularly in the sense that we responded expeditiously to every request in connection with this matter so that progress would not be retarded in any way. And I think that's been clear on the record thus far. And secondly, I have to say I didn't understand the characterisation of the Registry response to the request in July as being intractable. Particularly, what I heard was no travel unless necessary. It seems to me that situation could have been resolved with a determination of that including coming to the court as quickly as possibly. But then it turns out, in any event, that access to the OTP database, it seemed, was really not the issue here since other factors are identified as precluding that kind of visit until something else happens. So it seems that's a bit of a red herring under these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll invite the Registry to make any submissions on very short notice so as not to lose further time. That was your first preliminary matter. Mr. Lukic, you take the second?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and the third and the fourth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just need the assistance of the usher to distribute these copies to the booths and our court reporter, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any matter to be raised without the need of, perhaps, the third or the fourth?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Everything is on the same paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll patiently wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see that the papers were delivered, and I will start. So I will present three preliminary matters this morning. The first one is in section with the closing statement of Judge Orie from yesterday 22nd September 2015. On page transcript T39205, Judge Orie stated, and I quote: "Mr. Lukic, I again urge you to focus on what such a witness could bring us; that is, that she tell us about her expertise, that she does not start to evaluate the totality of the evidence. We not even knowing exactly always what it is that she has seen or what she has not seen. But if she moves away from her expertise, she should be considered a witness of fact and then we need a clear foundation of the sources of knowledge. And as usual, witnesses of fact are not expected to give an evaluation of the evidence." Your Honours, our ballistic experts visited all of the incident scenes and conducted their investigations and did their measurements. My question to you is: Does this instruction of yours means that they should not testify about their work in this regard? Because Ms. Subotic testified exactly about that before you gave this instruction. On transcript page 39203, the following was said, and I would quote, line 14 and further: "Q. So, did you manage to locate the other imprint? "A. In 2010 when we visited the location, there were two imprints in the parking-lot. They can also be found in the documents -- recorded in the documents created back in 2001 by the investigators. "Q. According to the documents you were able to review, when is the first mention of the second imprint? "A. We found it for the first time in 2001, meaning that it occurred sometime in between, between 1995 and 2001." Second issue in connection with the instructions by Judge Orie is the following. On page of our transcript 39200, that was yesterday, I would quote: "Judge Orie: Mr. Lukic, I am not telling you that you should not present other evidence. I am telling you that if you call a witness as an expert on ballistics, that that witness to draw all other kind of conclusions which are to be drawn by the Chamber, present the facts and leave the conclusions in the field of ballistics to expert and in other fields to the Chamber. "Please proceed." "Mr. Lukic:" -- that would be me. "Your Honour, Your Honour, it would be possible -- no, no, I have to respond -- "Judge Orie: Mr. Lukic -- "Mr. Lukic: It would be possible -- "Judge Orie: Mr. Lukic, please proceed. Next question to the witness, please. "Mr. Lukic: It would be possible if they were on the site at that time. They had to use everything that they had. "Judge Orie: Mr. Lukic, I told you - that's my ruling - that you should put your next question to the witness." In the course of this trial, we heard a large number of Prosecution witnesses, both factual and expert witnesses, who dealt with ballistics. The Defence concentrated almost all evidence of this kind and carried them through their experts on ballistics. For the proper functioning of our experts in ballistics, it is essential that they look at all the evidence in its entirety. Before this instruction given by Judge Orie, our expert witness, Ms. Subotic, testified about the case G-4, shelling in Dobrinja. She testified that the documents and the testimony of the witnesses of this point for this incident that occurred in 1993, only one shell impact crater was recorded at this location all the way until 2001. A second mortar shell impact crater appears in the documents only after the year 2001. Our expert has held that it is necessary to take into account this fact and she testified about the same. These are facts that the Defence holds the key to clearing up the case and rebutting the evidence presented by the Prosecution during its case. Is it the view of the Chamber and instruction to the Defence that our ballistics experts should just blindly carry out measurements without embarking on a whole evaluation of evidence that is necessary for them to locate and identify the forensic trace evidence with which they are to work as part and parcel of their ballistics review? With all due respect, the Defence does not agree with this position and will continue to present evidence that it considers relevant to the determination of the truth and directly related to the review and work performed by our expert witnesses. We consider ballistics experts not to be only mathematicians who deal with numbers, but they have an obligation to examine the evidence as a whole and to provide answers based on everything that they have studied, to support the findings and conclusions which they have. And I will now move to the third issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This issue, Mr. Lukic, I think I and my colleagues have carefully listened and we'll consider whether or not it needs any further response, because you have put a few questions, and I leave it at this moment to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The third issue is a matter of time required to properly present and examine our witnesses in court to demonstrate not only their conclusions but also the way our witnesses performed their ballistics review and reached their conclusions. The fact is the Defence estimated that for the examination of this witness it will take five hours. During the preparations here in The Hague, it turned out to be that this assessment was incorrect and that the Defence needs more time to complete the examination of this witness in a full and proper manner to appraise and assist the Chamber in dealing with rather lengthy and technical expert reports. The Defence points out that it does not seek to extend the time for the performance of the entire Defence case and points out that it will stay within the limits of 207.5 hours. Our question is who determines the manner in which the Defence uses their time, the members of the Defence team or someone else? Prosecution experts were not subjected to enforced reduction of the time for their testimony and indeed many Prosecution experts in direct examination had more than five hours without any similar instruction from the Chamber. Theunens, for instance, 7 hours; Butler had over 11 hours. Plus, I kindly note that multiple Prosecution experts presented evidence, including opinions, as to shelling in Sarajevo. Including, and this was Professor Higgs, for whom this Chamber did not limit him to prevent him from discussing the conclusions of others and then indeed he did analyse and give evidence about Bosnian police investigations and statements of witnesses. Thus, we are entirely concerned that now the Chamber is enforcing a different standard than that employed for the Prosecution experts on the very same subject matter. Thank you, Your Honours, for giving us the opportunity to address these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber, you're on your feet, to do what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If I could just make a few brief observations on the matters that just transposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber decides that you may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. We weren't informed of any of these matters just prior to court, but just some preliminary observations with respect to the first two issues raised by Mr. Lukic. It's the Prosecution's view, and it was our understanding, that the thrust of the Chamber's concern from yesterday was really a two-fold thing: One, whether or not the witness was encroaching on matters that really are in the purview of the Trial Chamber in the assessment of witness evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I really do not understand this exercise, that the Prosecution is telling us what the Chamber thought yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can say what they understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, of course they can't -- Mr. Weber has no pretension, I take it, to tell us what we meant but how he understood what we, as he thinks, we wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Exactly. It was just my observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And just on that, you know, it seemed to be coming up in the context, when it was happening, that there is a -- a difference between attacking the characterisation of evidence as being credible or not credible on another occasion as from the example that Mr. Lukic just actually used in court, where it was very specifically related to an observation by a witness as to the number of shells that were actually physically present and then subsequently finding out whether or not, in a site visit, such shells were actually there. So I think there is a distinguishing factor between those two. And then the other aspect, that at least appeared to me to be coming up in the context of court, there were just things that could be not within the area of expertise of this witness - medical evidence, FIFA rules - that we saw coming up during the course of the discussion of the G-4 incident. So at least from the Prosecution's view this appeared to be the types of things that were triggering the concerns at the time, which are also shared by the Prosecution if this was the case. With respect to expert Theunens just that -- that was commented on quickly. I just make the quick point, there was litigation before that and a discussion as to the reduction of the report or not, and then the Prosecution needing to lead extra evidence in terms of the extra timing for that report, so I just note that for the record. With respect to Higgs, our examination was rather limited and very focused and short, and it did focus on, of course, the Bosnian investigators' material and reports and the evidence that they collected during the course of their investigations. I believe the matters that are coming up in this expert report exceed that scope. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honours, about the FIFA rules. We just wanted to present what actually the witness showed to the investigator of the Prosecution, Mr. Hogan. He measured in his steps the length of that goal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- and we see the small one on the scene, and we see one in the back of that size on that. So we had to present, actually, what he showed on that only in the wrong place. That's why we have to -- had to put FIFA rules. If -- nobody needs FIFA rules, we can see the same goal in the picture which is part of the report, so I don't see anything improper if anybody uses FIFA rules. It's nothing that is hidden. Everybody can use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll later consider, Mr. Lukic, when -- by steps, the measurement of a goal is defined, whether there is or there is not a relevant link with FIFA rules. We would leave it to that for the time being. Those were your submissions. Now, there are two preliminary matters to be raised by the Prosecution. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And mine will be very short. Just to kind of keep track of our housekeeping and make progress with it as we go with the witness. The G-4 video with Investigator Hogan and Ismet Fazlic is available under 65 ter 22444A. The provisional number reserved for the video is D1244. We do have the -- the Prosecution just went ahead and cut the clips of the entire video and we have them present here in the court. If it's -- if it's ready to be tendered, then we -- I know it's technically a Defence exhibit, I don't know if the Defence wants to re-tender it, but I wanted at least to inform them at this time that that's available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say the whole of the video including all portions shown by the Defence is now available as 22444A.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And it was from the very beginning of the discussion of the G-4 to the end of the discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, how would you like to proceed with that video? The Prosecution -- Mr. Ivetic, yes. Mr. Ivetic, the whole of the G-4 part, apparently, is now available under this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't have a problem with that. The only concern I have is do the time-stamp entries that we used in court yesterday still apply to the selection made by the OTP in 22444A?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart is informing me that they do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if they would not, which I hardly dare to say when Ms. Stewart said that it was, then of course a table of concordance should be presented so that we know exactly what the -- and I think then it's appropriate for the Prosecution to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it will be your exhibit and as well the Prosecution's table of concordance if there is any problem remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it can be admitted. That means, Madam Registrar, that D1244 now consists of -- and I see it that the CD-ROM is presented to Madam Registrar at this moment, consists of 65 ter 22444A and is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second matter that the Prosecution had related to just the rolling notice of materials for this witness. Of course, the Prosecution is willing to be flexible and certain exhibits pose less of a challenge than others in terms of the late notification. I just kindly ask that if we get late notification of things, especially like happened last night, of longer videos that are 150 -- or an hour and 50 minutes long, that if there are some additional specification made by the Defence in terms of particularity, what part -- what time on the video, these are sometimes large compilations of many different incidents, and what part of the report specifically the portion that is being noted in terms of the time code or pages relate to. That would be greatly appreciated. With respect to the videos for yesterday, we ask that at least we receive that information before they are used in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Mr. Lukic, that to the extent possible you'll meet the request by --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in a position to provide Mr. Weber with this data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we -- I think if there are no other preliminary matters, then we could do two things, ask the witness to come in, but perhaps rather take the break now and start a bit earlier. We'll take a break, and we will resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's unfortunate that you had to wait a little bit longer. We had to deal with a few procedural matters first, and you were the victim. Mr. Lukic will now resume his examination-in-chief, and I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please let us go back to G-4, at least in your mind. I wanted to show you P872.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this exhibit, we can see it is entitled "Photo file," "Shelling," the 1st of June, 1993. Photographs taken on 21 November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next page, please. Can we see the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to your knowledge, who initiated this investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the investigation was conducted on the basis of the ICTY request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the site also visited by a representative of the OTP, of The Hague Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us see what we can find in this record of forensic investigation of the scene, especially because it was drafted two years after the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to see page 5 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S. [In English] Page 5 -- page 3 B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 3 in B/C/S, please. We have it in B/C/S. It's in the middle of the page -- sorry, the previous page first. It's page 3 in B/C/S. It's the previous page in English, I am sorry. Top of the page is in English. [Interpretation] In this paragraph, in the middle of the page in the B/C/S, we can see that it says: "A detailed forensic investigation of the scene of the attack revealed the following." Bullet point 1: "An artillery shell fell on the location of the parking lot in 3b Dobrinja neighbourhood." Let us now look at what was stated in terms of the second projectile, which is on the next page in the B/C/S but the same page in the English. [In English] Sorry, it is the next page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we see the following: "The point of impact of the second shell was not forensically examined due to the changed appearance of the soil adjacent to the parking lot (various agricultural plants have been planted there in the meantime)." What we can find in the indictment, what can we see there, how many projectiles and on what surface?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is specified that there are two shell imprints and that both can be found on the parking-lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at some footage next, and we will need only a few seconds of it. It is 1D05221.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I just ask you, there is a question mark in the transcript, page 23, line 7, "what we can find in the" and I think I heard you said "indictment." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then -- could you then further explore the answer in relation to the -- what we find in the indictment? Where the witness said that: "It is specified that there are two shell imprints and that both can be found on the parking-lot." Perhaps the witness could answer the question. Is it your testimony that the indictment tells us that imprints were found on the parking-lot and that there were two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add, both are in the -- on the asphalt, on the tarmac of the parking-lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether the indictment tells us that there were imprints of shells on the parking-lot and that there were two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 65 ter number that was just announced was 1D5221. We do not have this on our notification for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably I misspoke --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now it is on your list. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we should see this video from 2 hours, 7 minutes, 33 seconds, up to 2 hours, 7 minutes, 58 seconds. We will only rely on the picture, not on the sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there is no need --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution actually asked for -- I know what he's about to use, and we believe the sound is also relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sound or words spoken?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My recollection of the video is that there is sound, not necessarily words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Words, words, not sound. We are not leaning on sound -- on words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- because we don't have a transcript, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. So we'll ignore any words spoken unless the Prosecution insist on words spoken as well. And sound, of course, is sometimes also something which is not spoken but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let's have a look at it first and then we'll find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is not mute, definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we start, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report, did you rely on any stills from this footage, and if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We used the stills provided on images 32 and 33 showing blood traces or smears. In image 32, we can also see some shell traces; and in image 33, we can clearly where the shell had landed on the asphalt and to the right we see the trace of blood from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about images 28 and 29?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the same footage, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. 32 is not from the same angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, that's not what I mean. Let's look at the next thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's start with 2 hours, 8 minutes, 20 seconds, to 2 hours, 8 minutes, 26 seconds. Please bear with us. It isn't easy to find the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do images 28 and 29 have something to do with this part of the footage?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Images 28 and 29 are basically the same. They are related to the footage. However, image number 29 is simply zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'd like to tender the pieces of footage we have shown. We discussed it with my learned friend, Mr. Weber, and I believe he will have something to say about the footage when they rely on it later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for economy's sake, I think it would make sense just to have one number for the -- the relevant portions of this to the parties. We submit that would be time code 2 hours, 7 minutes, 33 seconds, to 2 hours, 8 minutes, 26 seconds. So we have no objection to that clip being cut for that time segment and being tendered at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We accept the way my learned friend proposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that we take that out as a separate exhibit, is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As one. So it's encompasses both these clips and [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in between.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the next one as well? So we'll wait --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we can have Defence number for the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, finally there -- the upload of the entire portion of the video, we are still waiting for that, but the time-frames here have been clearly defined. And we already reserve a number for this. Madam Registrar, the number to be reserved for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's reserved for the whole sequence of videos of which we have seen part of -- two, we have seen two parts. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] We'll look at another thing in the previous document, which was P872, the photo file and record created two years after the incident. Can we please have page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S version. The penultimate paragraph with the two bullet points in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is stated that it was established that the shell which hit the tarmac surface of the parking-lot was an 82-millimetre shell, and then the shell came in from the south-easterly direction of 110 degrees from the north. Did you try to verify the result of 110 degrees from the north?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your finding?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our finding differed from this one. Please bear with me. It is greater. Let me tell you the exact figure. Our finding is greater being between 139 and 150 degrees. We determined it in two ways: By direct measurement of the traces we found in September 2010, and by comparing it to the bearing of the parking line at the place of the traces, having previously determined the bearing of the parking-lot as per Google Maps which is just something we can see in image 35. The comparison I mentioned can be found in image 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Briefly tell us what your conclusion about the incident was.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Overall?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our conclusion about this incident was that there were many issues in trying to determine what the real situation was, starting first of all with the place of incident and followed by some missing information from the first police investigation, as well as the fact that UNPROFOR conducted an on-site investigation that we were unable to rely on because the reference trig points were some 200 metres away from the playing field. There was also a very particular or peculiar circumstance of having the police conducting a detailed investigation two years later. It was a very detailed, precise report, but they did not find the traces of the second mine. But all of us, starting with 2001 and ending in 2002, all of us found two traces; therefore, it was very difficult to make a positive decision bearing all this in mind. One thing is certain, though, which is that the game itself was not played at the location that was investigated but in the playing field next to it, which is something we discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to incident G-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, its page 51; in the B/C/S, 79.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to be sure what you said, "the game itself was not played at the location that was investigated." That was your conclusion on the basis of where cars were seen, where the poles of the goals were, is that where you rely upon when saying that: "One thing is certain ... that the game itself was not played at that location"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I rely on witness statements, the footage we saw today and yesterday, it was discussed at length, and of course the traces which were found or appeared. If the situation was described properly, they should have been there when Captain Houdet was there. He attended the scene but his co-ordinates were unclear. They took us 200 metres away from the area and we were unable to use them in any way in our investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties in understanding how, on the basis of traces you find on the floor -- you receive no interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties in understanding how, on the basis of traces you find on the floor, you can determine where they were playing football.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The traces of only one shell can be found on the ground on the day of the incident. However, all of the witnesses state, and it is not disputed, that two shells exploded. There is no trace of the other shell, as we can see on the TV footage. When you review the entire piece of the footage that was tendered, you will see that the whole parking-lot is visible but there are no extra traces; on the other hand, we said that there were no blood traces. Also, there were some mini goal-posts there, while in the playing field in the background you see a standard goal size. Also, we have the footage with Ismet Fazlic indicating the location. The investigators were brought in the same area, and two years later when they were there, there was still no traces of the second shell. Had the game been played there, two years later the traces of the second shell would have been present in the parking-lot. It is my impression that none of the investigators were taken to the playing field that we claim the game was played on. All of the material evidence indicate that the game was actually not played in the parking-lot. The investigators were told that it was somewhere on the site in the soil, but they didn't find anything in the parking-lot. Yet the witnesses claim that the shell landed only metres away from each other, all of those who survived the incident as well as a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's your conclusion on the basis of all that material.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we'll be talking about a case when on 12 July 1993, around 1527 hours, in Spasenije Babovic Street in Dobrinja, a shell -- an 82-millimetre shell fell. What was characteristic in your report, Ms. Subotic, in determining the facts?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, and the basic problem, was to locate the site of the incident. Although there was a police report, it contained contradictory information about the location where the shell fell. So we have one address, Branko Bujic alley, Josip Kras Street, Spasenije Babovic Street. So three different sites. Therefore, the basic thing that we had to start with was to locate the site precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how did you do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, wouldn't it be good for everyone to follow what we are talking about. It's about incident G-5, I take it, and I also see that paragraph 49 starts dealing with that incident. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's from the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the hard copy page is 81. I don't have it in e-court here at this moment -- at least I do not have it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is 81 in English and 79 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't receive interpretation at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please restart your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or perhaps you put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's try again. How did you manage to find the site and where was it? How many addresses did you mention in the report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mentioned three addresses in the report. We visited them all. By the way, we managed to find out that the Spasenije Babovic is no longer called that but Hakija Turajlic. And in that Hakija Turajlic Street, it was house number 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at 65 ter 11238. We have before us an official report about the incident of 27 -- sorry, 12 July 1993, and the report was made in August. We need page 3 in English and 5 in B/C/S. We see below the title "Official Report," when it was made, on the 9th of August. And it says that this incident took place outside the residential building in the alley called B. Bujic, number 6. Now we need paragraph 7 in B/C/S, which is on the same page. And in English, also on the same page -- [In English] Sorry. [Interpretation] I can't see it in English, in fact. That's the fifth paragraph in English. It says outside a private house in the alley B. Bujic, number 155, opposite another house in Spasenije Cane Babovic Street number 6. You said there were several addresses. You had a problem locating the site?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you look at picture 39, which was taken from Google Earth in the early -- B. Bujic and Spasenije Cane Babovic Street, these houses are not opposite each other. They are rather far apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the moment we don't need to take this document off the screen. I want to ask you which method did you find was used by the employees of the security services centre Sarajevo to determine the direction of the descent of the shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The method they mentioned in the official report, and it's again mentioned in some statements, is something that I saw for the first time. They mentally drew a line to designate the trajectory from the imagined site of explosion, and all these lines ended in the place where the shell exploded, and that's the mutilated body of an identified person who was thrown by the explosion and landed close to the fence. That type of explosion, I don't think I need to mention it, does not exist. And even if something like that existed, it could not be linked to the site where the corpse was found if the body had been thrown far from the site of the explosion. So it was totally unnecessary and completely useless for any kind of consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just get some clarity. Ma'am, you say that "they drew a line to designate the trajectory from the imagined site of explosion." What do you mean by "site of explosion"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the site of explosion is where the shell detonated, where the shell landed. In this case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we carry on with the sentence then. Then you say: "... and all these lines ended in the place where the shell exploded." It doesn't seem to be a line. It seems to a point. You are talking about a line from this point and it ends at this very point. It doesn't seem to be a line. It seems to be just a point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, maybe I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's extremely difficult to follow a thought that is so devoid of reason. What did he mean to say? He wanted to say that some lines that he saw on parts of the fence and cars, places where the shrapnel hit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I stop you, ma'am. Now you are telling about -- he said of a line. You are telling us that they drew a line in -- in their heads, an imaginary line. You are not telling us that somebody told you he drew a line, and I am trying to understand your thinking and your logic. You say they drew a line, imaginary line, from the site of explosion to the site where the -- where the thing detonated. Now, that seems to be the same point, and I'm asking you what he -- that's why I asked you what you mean by "site of explosion."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is one and the same point, and that's why I said I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that can't be a line. That can't be a line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, nobody drew any lines. They were all imaginary. The expert explains his work in the following way: He mentally drew lines from the place where he found traces of fragments and shrapnel, created by the explosion, and in his thoughts all these lines ended with the mutilated body where the centre of the explosion was. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Drew a line from there to where? Can you explain us where the line went to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in his head these lines were from where he saw defects on the fence. He didn't specify on cars and other places. And all these lines ended with the unidentified body lying next to the fence which - I am adding this now - which body was thrown by the explosion. It's extremely difficulty to follow this because this reasoning is flawed and technically impossible. If you need me to explain further, I am at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I -- well, I am hearing different explanations. Now you are mentioning fences and cars which you hadn't mentioned before, so I'm finding it difficult to understand what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll go through a document so I think it will be easier to understand soon. First we would offer this 11238 into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection. And that's the file for the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 11238 receives Exhibit Number D1251, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now can we have 1D05728, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'll take it that whatever mentally drawn lines are, that we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll read it in this next document, yes. The first one we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so apparently it's not only mentally, perhaps, but let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the statement of Hamdija Cavic taken by the OTP of this Tribunal. And in this statement, we need page 3 in English, halfway down the page, and also 3 in B/C/S, the fifth paragraph. I shall read what this witness says, [In English] in the middle of the page in both versions: [Interpretation] "Looking at all the damage on the fence and the car, I could see by the shape of the damage from which direction the shrapnel had come. When I drew imaginary lines from these defects, they all came together at one point, the mutilated body." [In English] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That makes it much better. I at least -- this is what this witness says, not what this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- tells us was imagined.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no -- yeah. I don't know how it was translated, but I had to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just would ask for the full reading of the paragraph. This is someone we haven't heard from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any problems if Mr. Lukic doesn't do it and you can do it later in --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if Mr. Lukic could follow your suggestion, he's free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can read till the end. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I forgot to read the last sentence in this paragraph: "It was without any doubt that the shell was fired from the direction we determined and wrote down in the report."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, now you left out the sentence in between, which starts: "Because of this ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I have it -- I read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, your assistant agrees with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, okay. Sorry. I was warned that I didn't read it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I missed another sentence, the one before the last. "Because of this, we concluded that the shell exploded on the body." So, Ms. Subotic, do you accept this method used to analyse this explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. So you don't accept it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is your main objection to the method used by the employees of CSB Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My main objection to the method used by CSB Sarajevo is that you cannot determine the place of explosion in that way, when the body was removed from the place of the explosion. If all these lines crossed at the same point, that's not where the explosion was. The body was not in the same place as the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This paragraph is not determining the place of explosion but the direction from which the fire came.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To establish the direction from which fire came, first of all you have to determine the site of the explosion. And then based on other material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, what did you establish and conclude, and in which way?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report itself states and also the photo documentation and the video recording made at this on-site investigation indicate sufficient elements to determine precisely where the explosion was and the direction of the shell. And let me also mention that when we were there in 2010, we found on the ground all the traces and we also identified the site of the incident based on the photo documentation, which was properly done, and based on the traces on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us then go back to your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one short question. You said the body wasn't -- had been removed. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photo documentation contains photos where the body is still there, still hasn't been removed, and it's indicated in the report. Picture 41, 44. In picture 44, the body is indicated by an arrow. It's between the Skoda car and the fence. And that is the corpse they used in the analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I may have to re-read portions of the transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I, for my clarity, just ask: What do you mean by "remove," Witness? Do you mean removed by the shell itself and thrown to another place, or removed later after the explosion by police people or somebody else? What do you mean by "removed"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the question as meaning whether the body was removed by the CSB people who prepared the report, and that's how I answered the question. No, the body is still there when the photograph is made. But the body had already been propelled and thrown by the explosion and that's where it came to land. And the explosion hit the right hip of that person, according to the documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm asking that because on page 39, line 6 and the following, you said: "My main objection to the method used by the CSB Sarajevo is that you cannot determine the place of explosion in that way, when the body was removed from the place of the explosion." You mean from -- removed from the place of the explosion, I understood the place of explosion to be that point where the body was thrown away from to the fence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter used this word "removed" to indicate that the body was removed by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In the sense, thrown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Witness, on the English channel they received some explanation from the interpreters. That's the reason why I asked you stop for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And this interpretation, this comment, clarified the matter for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's break time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly is. We'll take a break and we'll resume at 10 minutes past 12.00. The witness may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have on our screens 1D5498, please. And we need page 97 from this report in English and 96 in B/C/S, figure 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is figure 52 in front of you, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who took it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague and I, when together with the Defence team, we visited the incident locations in Sarajevo in 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The yellow line on the asphalt, what is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a measuring tape that we placed indicating the incoming trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you determine it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see in the photograph, we marked the still existing traces on the asphalt, and we used the method of central axis to place the tape in order for it to be visible. We determined the incoming trajectory by determining the bearing of the pedestrian path and its edge, and we can see the deviation from the pedestrian area to the incoming trajectory, including that the trajectory is in the direction of north or north --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat the side of the world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Witness, you are asked to repeat the last part of your answer. You said "from the north" and then you didn't finish the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said -- I don't know how far we got, but I'll start with the measuring tape and the traces again. I think it was 157, I started looking on Google Earth to locate the direction of the street. That is why I stopped and did not finish. It is 157. As you can see, some 20 degrees away it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say "as we can see," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were asked to repeat the last part of your previous answer. The sentence started: "We can see the deviation from the pedestrian area toward incoming trajectory, including that the trajectory is in the direction of north or ..." What did you say then? How did you conclude this sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it comes from the northerly direction, slightly towards the east. That was the part I did not complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The only problem for me is that looking at this photograph, I cannot make out, from what you have just told us, which is north, which is east, which is south.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolutely correct. That is why I stopped to look for another figure so as to assist you. It is figure 43 in the report, where we see the bearing of the street itself. When you look at that figure and compare it with this one, it is clear then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 88 from the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 89 in English and 88 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell us again what we can see here.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that when we look at figure 33 in the report, we can see the bearing, according to Google Earth, with relation to the place of incident, and it is 157 degrees compared to true north, and we come to the area -- the pedestrian area edge, which is some 10 to 20 degrees to the right. On this photograph, it is to the right, and on the previous to the left. It defines the incoming trajectory which is just off north in an easterly direction. So if we were to mark the incoming trajectory on this photograph, the one we could see on the previous one, it would be much clearer to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, [In English] can we have only one picture, let's say in English version, on our screen, and I will ask Ms. Subotic to draw that line since we don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To avoid any misunderstanding, it's figure 43, 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know it isn't easy, but try to do your best.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I failed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Wait a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you erase this so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More or less this is the direction shown by the measuring tape as the incoming trajectory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what does the second line indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was by accident that I touched the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can that be erased?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist in erasing what you by accident marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or maybe to erase everything and to have one straight line. Is this line good enough, or we should ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps for clarity's sake we could repeat this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Please, can you erase everything so that Ms. Subotic can draw next -- no, no, no -- yeah. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, is that then what you determined to be the direction of the incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. To the east compared to true north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if I look at the photograph, and you earlier said it's some 10 to 20 degrees, could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In what way? 10 to 20. It is as precise as we can gauge based on the existing evidence. 20, 30, there you go. Let's say between 10 and 30. That is why we did not determine it specifically in the report. We were unable to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it is definitely slightly off north towards the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I need some time to analyse that, but please proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we save this as the next Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Figure 43 on page 89 of the English version of the document 1D05498, marked by the witness, receives Exhibit Number D1252, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have picture or figure 52a on our screens. It's page 97 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What page is it in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 98 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, what did you determine on this photograph, and is it any different from what was previously shown?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we only have the incoming direction with a degree of tolerance or margin of error provided by Mr. Higgs in his report. We only added the right corner where we marked the boundaries of ABiH-controlled territory, and its bearing is up to 66 degrees, as we indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He determined that the incoming direction is north-east, and he accepted the results of Bosnian investigators' results. As for the material evidence, which is something we added, all that falls within the two blue lines, and we said it is to the east from true north up to -- and up to 66 degrees, the territory was controlled by the ABiH, as you can see in the caption.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly be asked to refrain from coughing into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, to the extent you can avoid coughing into the microphone, the interpreters would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, did you determine the separation line between the VRS and ABiH and how?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not determine that. This map was found in the Higgs report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This shell for which you told us came from the north-easterly direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just off north towards the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to be certain, it could not be west of north?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As Higgs ascertained, that is the Judge's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I didn't refer to Higgs in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked whether it could have been west of north, or are you certain that it's slightly east of north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are certain because we had evidence from the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have explained why you came to that conclusion. At least you've given us the dates, and I may revisit this matter later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you able to establish what was the closest position of the VRS compared to the direction you determined?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The closest positions were 8 to 9 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the maximum range of the mortar in question?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The maximum range is far below that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any military facilities close by?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were statements confirming that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which military facilities? Don't you know that from the top of your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, it would be too much for me to remember all that detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there was a command post some 100 to 150 metres away. Another facility that can be viewed as military was an entrance to the tunnel. The trenches, connecting trenches, according to witnesses' statements, were some 250 metres away. That is speaking off-the-cuff. I can't be more precise at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D5723.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before this comes up --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- I have a question with respect to the figure 52a we have in front of us. You say there, as an explanation of this figure: "The incoming direction of the shell drawn by Mr. Higgs, red, and the incoming direction north, north-east drawn on the basis of physical evidence, blue." What kind of physical evidence you are relying on? Could you briefly summarise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The type of traces left on the asphalt after the mine exploded. We showed you how we analysed it in figure 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, the traces on the asphalt. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One short follow-up question. You gave the blue line azimuth 66 degrees. That is what you established on that basis? Because you said "slightly east of north." Now, you go 66 degrees. That is more than two-thirds of a quarter of the compass. Is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
