utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's not in the transcript. Ms. Subotic explained that that's the area covered by ABiH, Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whatever -- Witness, I see azimuth is 66 degrees here on this figure 52a. Earlier you said it was just east of north. Now, when --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat? There were overlapping speakers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your last answer, because the interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the right-hand side corner of this image, we see delineated the area controlled by the ABiH and its limits are between 0 and 66 degrees. Our incoming trajectory is in a northerly direction just off to the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it falls within that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that point. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Any more questions by the Bench?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I certainly will have some more questions in relation to this later, but I at least now understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what 0 degrees and 66 degrees stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have -- yeah, we have on our screens 1D5723. We need -- it's testimony of Witness Ismet Hadzic in the case the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic. We need page 76 in e-court, and that would correspond to -- should correspond to the page 12215 from this transcript, line 13. This witness was asked and he marked a map, and I -- he said, I quote: "Q. You marked on the map with a dot and a number '4' beside it, a particular position. Could you tell us what that position is. "A. That's commander of the one of the battalions. I think that was the command of the 2nd Battalion." [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic said that there was a unit command post there, the unit is specified here. She also mentioned the entrance to the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, let me ask you this: Was this place shelled by the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but from another side. There are other traces but they were not caused by projectiles coming from this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've finished with this incident, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could I just have a reference if the counsel has the map that's being referred to by this individual uploaded, a 65 ter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, otherwise it will be difficult to comprehend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D01406, please. This is the map that Witness Ismet Hadzic marked during the trial in the case versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where can we find the number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, where can we find number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can this middle part be enlarged, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I mean the dot with the number 4 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know where it is, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know. That's why I asked the middle part of this map to be enlarged to be better visible, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, can you see it on the map? Can you see point number 4?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be around here, but I can't see it clearly. I don't see the figure 4, but I think it's around here where the arrow is, actually. The red part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Can you circle what you think that it is?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can this be saved as the next Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could the witness first explain what is the area she encircled? What is to be found there in your view?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you're on your feet but you're still silent. I wait until --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was waiting until -- I know Judge Fluegge posed a question, so I didn't to want interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You encircled a certain feature, but I -- what is it? What in your view is situated there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, it is the battalion command on the ABiH side that we mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe the document had been tendered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- and that's why I raise -- Your Honour, with the caveat -- I understand the witness has marked on it and we now need to admit the screen capture of what's marked there. I do have an express concern based on what was just led from the witness's testimony and what may be in-court markings versus pre-markings and multiple different numbers on it. So it's not clear -- I guess the objection in part -- concerned in part as to the reliability of what we are admitting and what the record is in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because the map was introduced by you, Mr. Lukic, and exclusively by you, and then you read a portion of what was to be seen at number 4, and then you asked the witness whether she could circle 4 and then asked what that was. Now, as leading as can be, I would say, the witness only said that a person was not shelled but -- or was shelled, I don't know, but that was the initial question. And then you led her skillfully to the answer, and it was leading as can be, but Mr. Weber does not object. Therefore, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to succinctly put it: I am not objecting because it's an in-court marked document by the witness. We do have a reservation because there is a witness who has not testified in the trial, evidence that has not been heard by the Chamber, and the clarity in terms of that evidence as what's been posed we do have concerns -- reservations about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the expression of concerns and reservations are not an obstacle to admission. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photo of document 1D01406 with green witness remarks receives Exhibit Number D1253, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would just add that this was the Prosecution witness in another case, and if they have any doubts they should raise it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or not maybe today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not about doubt. You totally misunderstood the concerns expressed by Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But Ms. Subotic previously, we have it on the record, testified that she knows that in that area was a command of one of the practice brigades and entrance to the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you showed -- and then you read to her a statement which says where exactly it is to be found; namely, at number 4. Then this witness tried to find number 4 on that map, and then asked what was there, she referred to what that other witness in that other case had said already. And that's leading and it's no more no less. It's not -- it's admitted into evidence. But please try to understand, it really is leading, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it leading if it's in the report already?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. You have --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not taken us to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is in the report, in the report we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I will give a footnote, just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then it's still leading, but then you say it's already somewhere there. We'll carefully check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- it's footnote 195 from this report that we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 195. We'll have a look at it. It's admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In front of us we have a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The report we are discussing today, Your Honour. You are right. It's 1D5498. Footnote 195.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that -- did that include the testimony of that witness? Is that part of it as well, transcript pages, or just the document? If you would read the footnote --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- it is testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including with the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both. 195 is testimony, it's 1D5723. And since it's testimony in front of this court, we cannot offer it into evidence. We have to read it. And 196. And also map under 195. Under 1D1406. Everything in the same footnote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yell. So you say it's totally useless to present all this. You could just have tendered this as sources. But let's leave it, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's admitted. The questioning as such was leading, but we do understand that the witness had referred to -- by reference, not lines read, but has referred to the same material which you now put to her. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would move now to G-6 incident. It's page 99 in English and page 98 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the incident when three mortar shells fell in the area of Alipasino Polje on 22 January 1994. The first fell on Rade Koncar Square, the second outside a building in Cetinjska 3, and the third outside a building in Klare Cetkin Street number 4. In two police reports it is said that the shells had fallen and exploded in these places. You have before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move one page forward. See picture 33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 33 or 53?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did I say -- no, it should be 53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, what did you note as a problem in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main problem in this case is that the finding of police investigators was different from the scene of crime technicians' findings, the crime-scene officers who analysed the shell traces in this incident, and the final finding was given by Captain Verdy. The investigators established that in Klare Cetkin Street and the other street there were 82-millimetres shells, and in Rade Koncar Square --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, stop. You are invited to slow down because your speed of speech --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- causes difficulties for the interpreters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Rade Koncar Square, the shell was 120-millimetres. The difference: UNPROFOR, that is to say, Captain Verdy, was of the opinion that three 120-millimetre shells exploded, and the scene of crime officer who investigated the scene thought the same; whereas investigators found that in Cetinjska and Klare Cetkin streets it was 82-millimetre shells, whereas only the Rade Koncar Square shell was 120 millimetres. That was the main reason why we had to investigate what really happened. Maybe I should add that Mr. Higgs put his trust in Bosnian investigators without noticing that even they are not in agreement with their own scene of crime technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the report of Captain Verdy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see in e-court 65 ter 10570. [In English] Can we have the next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recognise this document, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the most important thing about this report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The key thing in this report is that Captain Verdy provided a detailed crater analysis, determined the directions, provided photographs, and he even estimated the angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you certain that we have the right version on the screen? There is no B/C/S. I see a French document which doesn't correspond with the English. The witness said that she recognises the B/C/S version, but there is no ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said so based on the first things in the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a B/C/S version? Because I saw one during our preparations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we have a French and an English version apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is no space for the third one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there is space in e-court but I don't know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And they are not identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it is in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you check?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes we have three versions in e-court. So they are not the same documents and they are not -- and the one is in French and the other is in English. The content is totally different. Mr. Lukic, perhaps you reorganise your --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the Prosecution 65 ter number so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it that you have checked before you'd use --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- this sloppy material, if it is. This seems to be the one. This seems to be to -- we now have to the left what seems to be an original French version, and to the right we have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we were just checking and there might be -- there is multiple versions of this material on our exhibit list. To suggest 65 ter 18013, it appears to be the same document but has a B/C/S translation attached to it. So there is an original French version, there is an English translation for the related pages that are in French, and then there is also a B/C/S version and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it covers exactly the same in totality?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, we just verified the ERNs, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would accept kind offer from my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we then look at the number just referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have told us what Captain Verdy did. What were his findings consistent with? Did Verdy confirm some Bosnian investigators' findings and not others?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Verdy confirmed that the findings of the scene of crime officers; namely that all the three shells that fell in this area were of 120 millimetres, and he's not in agreement with the directions determined by the CSB investigators. Their directions were Nedzarici - namely, the Institute for the Blind - whereas Verdy determined in mils the south-west direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you direct us to the respective page of this document where we can find anything about Captain Verdy and his conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2, please. And conclusion continues on page 3 as well. And next page in B/C/S as well so Ms. Subotic can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see here, Ms. Subotic, the conclusions in mils. Did you convert it into degrees?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These mils are 236 degrees and the other indication in mils is 239 degrees. That's on page 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S, you mean. Could you tell us the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, just as a reference, as instructed by Judge Orie, I shall say that Exhibit P865 speaks to this. We have the difference in calibres, that's page 1 in English and page 5 in B/C/S, 120 millimetres. Page 2 in English, second paragraph from the top, in B/C/S/ page 4, that last paragraph, there is a reference to an 82-millimetre shell. Again in English page 3, the first and third paragraphs, and page 5, paragraph 3 in B/C/S, another reference to an 82-millimetre shell. Page 4 in English and page 7 in B/C/S, a document from the higher court in Sarajevo mentioning a 120-millimetre shell. Page 7 in English and page 12 in B/C/S, a reference to a 120-millimetre shell. Page 8 in English, page 14 in B/C/S, under item 6, record of the crime scene inspection of the site. Paragraph 3 in English, and page 15 in B/C/S, an 82-millimetre shell is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I am not able to follow. What are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I have to go to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I just want to know what kind of document you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's P865, it's the evidence in our case, the Prosecution evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is compilation of the documents that deal with this incident in Klare Cetkin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This was missing in your introduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought that I said it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry if I missed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that you pointed at pages where you found evidence which was not consistent as to the calibre and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Different calibres, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Different calibres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you pointed at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- variety of the calibres that are mentioned in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then again English page 8, the last paragraph, B/C/S page 16, paragraph 1. It says -- it mentions both, 120 millimetres and 82 millimetres, that the fin is from one and markings from the other one. And on page English version 9 and B/C/S version 16, it's mentioned that it's 120-millimetres mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now a question for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, did you come to any conclusion, why are there discrepancies, why some of the calibres shown inaccurately?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we determined which calibres were involved exactly. Based on a very detailed analysis reflected in our report, we noted that the Klare Cetkin Street shells, mines, and in the other street were 82 millimetres. The exact trajectory of descent was established back in 2003, and even Mr. Sabljica agreed with them in court because we confronted him with our measurements, and we concluded that after the entire analysis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for about the best page and a half, there has been different concepts coming up on the record between trajectories, direction to fire, now angles of descent, and calibres, and they are getting a little muddled, I believe, on the record. If we could be clear as to what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The issue was calibres. Could you please, for the time being, stick to that, Witness. And when you say "even Mr. Sabljica agreed with them in court because we confronted him," did you confront him in court with anything, or do you mean by "we" the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether you meant --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the Defence, but I was assisting the Defence, sitting in the courtroom, and I participated in this examination, that's why I said "we." We put to Mr. Sabljica our measurements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no need at this moment to further elaborate on it. I have got an answer to my question. Could you limit yourself to the calibres. But at the same time, Mr. Ivetic, I see we are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic is sitting. This is Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are all tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're all in the same line, drawn imaginary --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of fire, you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- imaginary line --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fire coming from that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The source of fire still to be established. It's time for a break, unless you could finish in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour. We can go to the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we would like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's me that has to apologise for the late start, not the Chamber as a whole. Could the witness be escorted into -- unless, Mr. Tieger, you would need more than one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Maybe slightly more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll wait for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom until you have addressed the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Two matters I'd like to raise. The first is the following: On the 15th of December, the Defence re-filed its motion to re-add a witness to its witness list and admit the evidence pursuant to 92 bis. We responded to their original motion to do so on the 1st of September. This has been a series of transactions as the Court may recall. But in this case, our review of their current re-filing reveals that paragraph 3 of our earlier response in which we sought the redaction of evidence related to acts and conduct is now moot because that evidence has, in fact, been redacted. But our review of the motion itself and our response reveals that our positions as set out otherwise remain. So if it meets with the Court's approval with that understanding, particularly with regard to paragraph 3 of our response, we would propose to rely on our earlier filed response and not go through another filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any objection against part of the admission -- of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not have objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then this is an oral response saying that you stick to your old position apart from that one issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The second matter is this. As we're all aware, we recently passed the dead-line set by the Chamber for the Defence to file any remaining evidentiary motions including 92 bis or quater motions not directly connected to the testimony of upcoming witnesses. We have noted the absence of any bar table motions which would, on its face, seem to fall within the category of "any remaining evidentiary motions." We don't know whether the Defence intentionally declined to file bar table submissions or whether they regarded the instructions as not encompassing such submissions, and in addition, we don't presume to tell the Trial Chamber what was definitively encompassed by those instructions. Instead, we raise the matter simply to ensure that there are no unnecessary surprises and accompanying delays in the waning days of the case. Not only would a large bar table submission risk delaying the conclusion of the case on its own, but it would also potentially affect the rebuttal calculus and thus risk further delay to the closing date. So if the issue is resolved, then no problem. But one way or another, we seek to avoid the risk of large submissions at the end of the case that require corresponding time both to respond and to rule on and might needlessly protract the case. So we thought it prudent at this stage to raise the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If it's okay, I can perhaps give a more succinct response since I deal with the filings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, usually it's given by counsel but not by a member of the Defence team, but if Mr. Lukic invites you to do that, then we'll listen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can, of course, clarify and perhaps because -- well, Your Honours will remember your guidance at the beginning of this case, that the parties should file their bar table submissions at the end of their cases, so we did not foresee your 18 September dead-line as to 92 bis or 92 quater motions as encompassing the bar table submissions. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the language we used was "all evidentiary submissions" and not limited to 92 ter and 92 bis or quater.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe it was relating to witnesses, but we can check that. But in any event, the Prosecution received approximately a month or two after their last witness to do bar table submissions so we think it's in the interests of justice and fairness that the Defence have a similar ability that the Prosecution enjoyed. We can't change the rules at the mid-game to have the Prosecution have one set of rules and the Defence to have another set of rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what could we expect? I mean for scheduling purposes, it's good to know whether -- and that's what, I think, what Mr. Tieger was hinting at, is what is there to be still expected? No further -- I think there are two filings for witnesses which were late, and we'll consider whether -- we have not heard from the Prosecution yet that they would oppose, despite being slightly late, being admitted. But in that respect, that's the first part. Is there anything else which would --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We do intend to be filing a bar table submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We haven't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But no further witnesses, therefore. That's clear then. 92 bis, 92 ter, 92 quater --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is that one that I mentioned of a Rule 70 witness which is in the process of being finalised to be filed. We are converting him from what had been perceived to be a 92 ter to a 92 bis. That's the only one that comes to mind as being a 92 bis, quater, in that category. So all other witnesses will be presented in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then to the extent our dead-line covered witnesses, I think it was limited to 92 bis and 92 quater as my colleague tells me, not necessarily to a 92 ter if a witness is on the witness list. Now bar table motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What could we expect there?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We anticipate filing a bar table motion. We have not completed nor even made much headway in terms of examining all of the documents that are the potential for the bar table motion, that is to say that are on both parties Rule 65 ter lists. We are in the process of analysing all those and hope to have a filing that will encompass everything that we want to be admitted. And we are preparing a schedule for that that we were going to present essentially asking for the same time-period that the Prosecution had upon the end of its last witness in court, who was the expert Theunens, and the filing of their last bar table submission, which I -- I again hate to speak off the top of my head as to dates, but I believe it was a month or two after that witness that the final bar table submission was filed. And there were several that were filed with multiple documents. I think one had 700 documents that I had to respond to. So I understand the concerns by the Prosecution. They are the same concerns that the Defence had to suffer under and do, and we're asking for a fair opportunity to make use of bar table submissions in the same manner as the Prosecution was allowed to do in their case as we believe -- no, the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you made your point clear, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider it. Two matters: First the interpretation of evidentiary motions; second, the -- the bar table motions, how that -- how exactly we dealt with that and how we will deal with it now. No further matters? Could the witness then be escorted into the courtroom. And the Chamber will also consider, Mr. Ivetic, whether we'll ask for further details such as an assessment of whether it will be 200 documents or 2.000 documents of all those that you are still considering.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't want to take additional time to raise the issue of the circumstances in which the Prosecution bar table motions were filed or at what time or how many. It didn't seem the appropriate time. But if that's going to play a role in the Court's consideration of the schedule, I'm happy to respond at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic referred to how we treated the Prosecution and gave a short sketch of that. If you think that it's -- it needs in any way any further explanation or elaboration, then of course in due course -- because the Chamber will consider of course everything that was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then in due course you could give us any further elaboration or clarification you may need useful. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have 1D5498 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I rise just because we are moving on to a different document. On the screen before the break with was 65 ter 18013. I just want to alert the Chamber that that a version of that document has been admitted already as Exhibit D178. However, it does not have -- that admitted version does not have all the related translations that were being looked at at the time of trial which are all available under 65 ter 18013. So we have no objection to replacing Exhibit D178 with the 65 ter used in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think it would be best to have the original French and then the English and the B/C/S translations there. So there 65 ter 18013 should now replace what is now known as Exhibit D17 -- D178, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the extent necessary, not only it should replace but the Registry is instructed to replace.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, we are now on incident G-6. I hope you have your report in front of you on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 107 in English, 106 in B/C/S. Photograph 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Apart from you, what do we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see the marked traces of the detonation of the shell, and we see the tape stretched in the direction of the central axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On what basis did you make your conclusions in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, as we can see on the picture, we made our conclusions about the direction of fire and the calibre of the shell based on the size of the crater and the traces of fragments. You can see they reach up to 3 metres, almost up to the middle of the street, and it was rather simple to determine directions which we show here with this white tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us now, is it different to what the Bosnian investigators determined?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's different. We determined 237, which means south-west. And they determined direction west, Nedzarici, Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have enlarged only English picture on our screen. I would ask Ms. Subotic to mark that picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, what do you want me to mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark on this photograph the direction established by the Bosnian investigators who worked on this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate what angle you approximately took? It looks to me as something close to 50, 60, or 70 degrees from the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they determined the direction of Nedzarici, where the angle is 270 degrees, and we established a direction of 237 degrees. That's how the difference should be shown. And this arrow should come from the west, the westerly direction. It's very difficult to show it precisely in this slanted projection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. So the difference is, as a matter of fact, 33 degrees, and you intended to depict a difference in direction of 33 degrees and not 50, 60, or 70.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help, Your Honour. We would just offer this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photo on page 107 of the document 1D05498 receives Exhibit Number D1254, Your Honours, marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at page 72, line 21, there is a angle quoted as 270 degrees. It if counsel could just -- or the witness even, I'm having trouble finding that in the report or documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could assist, please. Or if the witness could assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the findings of the Sarajevo police, it says that the direction was "west, Nedzarici, Institute for the Blind." The exact azimuth for the Institute for the Blind concerning this incident is 266 degrees, and the exact azimuth of west is, as we all know, 270 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we can find that at page 106 of English version and 105 of B/C/S version. It's in the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you are referring to the?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To this report that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But to the e-court pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: E-court pages, yes, Your Honour. 106 in English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move there, we should admit this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was admitted, yes. Just [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- said it was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Ms. Subotic, did the Bosnian investigators use the same method as you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although they did not document it in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they draw on a sketch what they found on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to ask you something about the second shell that exploded in Cetinjska Street. Tell us briefly what was characteristic of that shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that place, also the investigators claimed that it was an 82-millimetre shell, the scenes of crime officer said it was a 120-millimetre shell, and Captain Verdy said the same. Captain Verdy gave an accurate azimuth, and they stuck to the Nedzarici direction, the Institute for the Blind. I mean, we have the same discord, the same disagreement as we had about the point of landing of the shell. That's what I would call characteristic of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at page 111 from document 1D5498 in English. And page 110 in B/C/S. We need picture 60. [In English] Actually, we would ask figure 60 to be enlarged only from the English version, to have only that on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see Mr. Hogan on this picture. And what else?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this photograph, we see the site of the landing of the shell in Cetinjska number 3. We see very clearly the trace of the explosion on the asphalt. Why did we do this? Because that street, when we visited, had been paved over so we didn't see the original traces. They were not there. Then we used the footage of Mr. Barry Hogan, which was made in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, would you be able to mark the direction determined by the Bosnian investigators concerning the incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Using the same photograph, could you mark the direction determined by Captain Verdy in his report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first line, as the angle determined by the Bosnian investigators, mark it with a 1 and the other one with a 2.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you try to determine the incoming direction of the shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did try to do that based on the footage, and our result was very close to that of Captain Verdy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The direction being the one marked with the number 2 on the photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How do you explain these discrepancies if the same method was used?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will need some more specific parameters to respond. Given the fact that the same method was used but it was not documented how it was used, I wouldn't be able to give you a full reply because I would need to go through it all to be able to tell you where the mistake lay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your view, what did you determine? From which territory did the projectile come?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having examined the traces we had in detail and having conducted an analysis on the basis of Barry Hogan's footage, we determined that Captain Verdy accurately measured the incoming trajectory. But he based his calculations on some wrong photographs based on the asphalt traces at the location where the shells landed. When the error is corrected, we arrive at 236 and 239 degrees. Since both Captain Verdy and we determined that, based on the characteristics of the weapons, the shells were fired from one and the same weapon, it was our conclusion that the shells were fired from an area close to the Institute for the Blind, and the distance is 3.720 metres. We were able to be so precise simply because of the fact that the shells were fired from the same weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would just offer this into evidence, and if you have more questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the course of the examinations, I haven't been objecting to leading. However, there are assumptions of facts that the Bosnian investigators determined the direction of fire to be. I don't understand her report to exactly be saying that. And with that caveat, though, I understand she's marked the photo and it's going to get admitted, but just based on the record, we do not accept the -- the leading nature and the assumption of the direction determined by the Bosnian investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we -- I offer this one into evidence, and then we'll move to the next photo and it might be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's why I asked Madam Registrar to provide a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Figure 60 of page 111 of the English version of the document 1D05498 with witness remarks receives Exhibit Number D1255, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1255 is admitted into evidence. Witness, could you explain a bit more in detail, "that the shells were fired from an area close to the Institute for the Blind and the distance is 3.720 metres." And you say: "We were able to be so precise simply because of the fact that the shells were fired from the same weapon." Now, this suggests that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would know --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was recorded that way. Its not "Institute for the Blind" but "UPI," "UPI."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That doesn't change my question that much. Because if you have to establish from where a mortar was fired, to say we can be very precise because they came from the same weapon, if you don't know where that weapon is, the fact that you have two impacts does not help you greatly, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not provide all the details in my answer but I will do so now. We had two strikes within a short period of time. The ranges of both shells differ by 15 metres. For the mortar in question, the degree of error is 20 metres. Therefore, from two different locations you could not have two shells in such a small area from the same direction in the same VD --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness doesn't explain the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain what VD stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it is a characteristic of dispersion by distance. Perhaps I should have explained that. It is according to the tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you also explain to me what degree of error you had in your mind? You said it was 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 20 metres comes from the tables of dispersion that relate to the shells of 120 millimetres. The range difference between the two shells, which landed in a very short period of time, is 15 metres, meaning that it would be a strike within a single VD, making it very precise even by mortar standards -- or single mortar standards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But shouldn't you then know whether there was any adjustment at the firing position, any adjustment to the angle of firing or -- in order to draw such conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not this conclusion. But the adjustment of direction of firing was calculated and we processed it because the two shells landed along the axis of 200 metres with the same range. Expert Higgs also stated that whoever was firing those shots must have made firing corrections; however, this does not make our conclusion that it was fired from the same weapon any more questionable. The same conclusion was reached by Verdy and Higgs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was not asking you about the -- whether the conclusion that it was fired from the same weapon, whether there was any problem with that. I asked you how from that fact you could be so precise of 3.720 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very simple. When you have the fact that the same weapon was used to fire them, then you simply draw the directions as defined on the location where the shells landed, according to the bearing, and they must insect at a certain point. That gives you the distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that. But you were saying 3.720 metres. Earlier you explained to us that on the basis of the pattern it would be -- and you remember that other case where you said, well, 10 to 20 degrees it was. So there is apparently quite a margin of the direction of the origin of fire, which, as far as I understand, would have an impact on the accuracy and the position of the distance, that's where the two lines cross.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in this case. Because at the end of our analysis, we established that the bearings taken on the spot were accurate. They were measured by Captain Verdy after the incident. We relied on his results, and based on those we reached a conclusion about the place of firing. All the checks we ran differed very slightly, and we chose to believe his data because he was on the spot immediately after it happened as opposed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you say then the origin of fire, the direction of the origin of fire, as established by Verdy, there is no margin of error there, that's fixed. You rely on that and that's for certain. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We relied on his results as he measured them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your results are as good as his results are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is only a minor difference and we chose to trust him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And on what basis do you choose to trust him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First and foremost, because our assessment of the incoming trajectory was made on the basis of Barry Hogan's footage because the traces were no longer there, the road had been paved over when we came. When we established that direction and when we realised that there is only a few degrees difference, as in the previous location, we believed it to be more correct to take his results given the fact that he visited the scene. Things would not have been much different, only by a few degrees, if we had relied on ours, but we believed that it would be more correct and accurate to rely on the measurements made on the spot immediately after the incident rather than ten years later. We also analysed the footage and we found it to be more technically accurate to do it this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the results of Verdy were the best you had at that time and that's the reason why you thought it best to rely on those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they matched almost to the degree with what we were able to check on the spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. No, we should not proceed as a matter of fact. We should, as a matter of fact, adjourn for the date. We are not sitting tomorrow because it's a UN holiday, and since we are not sitting on Friday and have decided quite a while ago that we would not compensate for that one non-sitting day this Friday, it means that we will resume next Monday. I again instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony or to communicate in any other way about your testimony, and we'd like to see you back Monday morning and that will be the -- let me just make no mistakes. That will be the -- I'm saved by Madam Registrar. Monday, the 28th of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to very briefly deal with one procedural matter for which we have to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll adjourn for the day, and we'll resume Monday, the 28th of September, 2015, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of September, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25
